findings.title: Microsoft 365 Status: issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region
findings.summary_md: Microsoft's official Microsoft 365 Status account said it was investigating reports of users unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods, first scoped to the Americas. While working to mitigate, the account confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region and pointed to the incident under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center and status.cloud.microsoft.

findings.title: Microsoft 365 Status: elevated load driven by servers being unexpectedly unavailable
findings.summary_md: Microsoft said the elevated load on its infrastructure was not driven by an increase in traffic but by a number of servers becoming unexpectedly unavailable and straining the remaining infrastructure. The post attributed the server loss to failures of automated service health checks and referenced incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821.

findings.title: Microsoft 365 Status: failed health checks may originate from a specific component
findings.summary_md: Microsoft said it had not identified any recent change correlated with the start of the impact, but that its investigation indicated the failed health checks may originate from a specific component responsible for processing server health. It was testing a configuration change and working an alternate health check method to return affected servers to service under EX1550543 and MO1550821.

findings.title: Widespread Microsoft outage takes down Outlook and other 365 services
findings.summary_md: CNBC reported a Microsoft outage on Thursday 12 November 2026 affecting users of Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365. Microsoft 365 had drawn nearly 50,000 reports on Downdetector alongside problems reported for Teams, with users across multiple regions affected.

findings.title: Outlook, Teams and More Microsoft Programs Disrupted by Outage
findings.summary_md: The New York Times reported that the outage began on the afternoon of Thursday 12 November 2026 as workers and offices around the world reported problems with a range of Microsoft 365 tools and apps, including email and chat software. The report described a broad disruption to Microsoft's hosted productivity services.

findings.title: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune
findings.summary_md: The Register reported that a core process on some servers became overwhelmed, causing servers to fail automated health checks and go offline, with the incident running past 12 hours. Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, Defender for Office 365 and administrative tools such as Intune and the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center were unavailable. Microsoft's status updates stated that actions taken so far had not provided the anticipated relief and that no recent change had been correlated with the start of the impact.
